decisionKernel.ownership: A separately versioned package under axm-arc is the initial canonical authority. It has its own package manifest, conformance vectors, receipt schema, semantic version, and dependency boundary. Arc and World consume the exact same package source. Later extraction to a dedicated repository is a packaging decision, not permission for duplicate law.
invariants: actors and capacity units use opaque domain identifiers
work contracts carry constraints, resources, risks, and candidate options
feasibility produces exact rejection reasons
expected effects name model and policy versions
selection records assumptions and authorizing authority
externally observed outcomes are first-class inputs
expected-versus-actual reconciliation never invents attribution
decision receipts are immutable, canonical, versioned, and replayable
state transitions validate against the selected option and observation
next feasible options derive from the resulting state
conformance: budget capacity capability risk and approval vectors
canonical decision receipt and replay vectors
Arc and World byte-equivalent canonical decision facts

invariants: operation identity is derived from canonical prepared facts
every participant names the exact parent run digest it consumed
transport may repeat but application is idempotent by operation identity
a causally stale operation is refused before state mutation
prepare records intended effects without pretending they already occurred
commit records each participant application separately
partial commit is represented explicitly and never rewritten as atomic success
compensation is a new consequence-bearing operation rather than history deletion
return preserves both sovereign state sets and all unknown memory
forked histories remain distinct until an explicit reconciliation operation
